prisoners.name: Napoleon Jones
prisoners.description: Napoleon Jones is a US Navy veteran who recorded a police traffic stop in Sussex, Wisconsin, on May 4, 2025. Deputies subsequently stopped his vehicle, handcuffed him and took him to Waukesha County Jail. Reporting describes five hours in custody before release without citations or criminal charges. His federal civil-rights complaint alleges that the stop and arrest were retaliation for recording police. The complaint reproduces a sheriff's supervisor memorandum acknowledging that the traffic stop was unlawful and Jones could not be compelled to identify himself. Jones also alleges that deputies later used Flock license-plate searches to track his vehicle in retaliation for his complaint. Those retaliation claims are allegations in his civil lawsuit, not findings of a final judgment.

cases.charges: Arrest for alleged resisting and obstructing; no criminal charges forwarded
cases.sentence: Released without citations or criminal charges after approximately five hours in Waukesha County Jail. The December 1, 2025 complaint in Jones v. Shayhorn, Eastern District of Wisconsin, 2:25-cv-01886-LA, alleges retaliation for filming police and quotes a supervisor's May 10 memorandum describing the May 4 decision not to forward charges and to release Jones. Reason, September 2, 2026, independently reports the five-hour custody period. No prison sentence imposed. The detention is not rounded to a full day in the imprisonment counter; the civil lawsuit is separate from this arrest case.
